verdicts.quote: “Ahrefs Connect uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE).”
verdicts.reason: Ahrefs offers a first‑party OAuth flow for third‑party apps via Connect; for a multi‑tenant toolkit this is the appropriate primary method even though API keys also exist. ([docs.ahrefs.com](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/ahrefs-connect/docs/oauth-guide))

verdicts.quote: “Getting started… 2. Apply to join … 3. Get credentials and implement OAuth … 5. Submit for review and go live.”
verdicts.reason: OAuth client credentials require joining the Ahrefs Connect program and passing review; dev creds aren’t self‑serve. (Note: direct REST API keys are self‑serve but on paid plans.) ([docs.ahrefs.com](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/ahrefs-connect/docs/introduction))

verdicts.quote: “API v3 allows you to pull data from the Site Explorer, Keywords Explorer, SERP Overview, Rank Tracker, Site Audit… [plus other endpoints].”
verdicts.reason: Docs show many product areas and management endpoints; e.g., Site Explorer alone lists “Endpoints 46,” indicating dozens of resources across the suite. ([docs.ahrefs.com](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/api/docs/introduction))

verdicts.quote: “Ahrefs provides a hosted MCP server that allows users with a Lite plan or higher to connect their Ahrefs account to supported AI tools.”
verdicts.reason: This is a vendor‑maintained, hosted MCP server with official docs and connection URL. ([docs.ahrefs.com](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/mcp/docs/introduction))

verdicts.quote: “You’ll need an API key to send requests via Ahrefs API v3… Create and manage existing API keys in Account settings.”
verdicts.reason: Buildable today via documented REST API and self‑serve keys; caveats: access is plan‑gated (“Ahrefs API is available on eligible paid plans”) and the preferred OAuth route is partner‑gated with an approval step. ([docs.ahrefs.com](https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/api/docs/api-keys-creation-and-management))
